appraisal_events.evidence: "Je vous crois un peu qu'elle est belle ! Mais on n'avoue pas qu'on ne connaît pas la sonate de Vinteuil, on n'a pas le droit de ne pas la connaître," and later, faced with Swann's specific remark, a stock brush-off: "on ne perd pas son temps à couper les cheveux en quatre ici, ce n'est pas le genre de la maison."
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin's claimed authority on Vinteuil collapses into ready-made phrases and a dismissive brush-off the moment Swann asks something substantive, exposing her admiration as fashionable pose rather than real understanding.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Ah ! c'est tout à fait une très grande machine, n'est-ce pas ? ... mais c'est la très grosse impression pour les artistes" -- vague art-jargon offered instead of any real answer, part of a group the narrator says "furent incapables" of answering Swann's questions.
appraisal_events.explanation: The painter's grandiose but empty phrase-mongering is presented by the narrator as of a piece with the salon's hollow profession of admiring Vinteuil.

appraisal_events.evidence: He watches Mme Verdurin "avec une admiration béate et un zèle studieux" amid her flood of ready-made phrases, then, once the more knowing "fidèles" have dispersed, ventures a borrowed phrase like "un nageur débutant qui se jette à l'eau... mais choisit un moment où il n'y a pas trop de monde pour le voir": "c'est ce qu'on appelle un musicien di primo cartello !"
appraisal_events.explanation: Cottard is drawn as a credulous disciple of Mme Verdurin's formulas and as a nervous novice risking a borrowed bit of sophistication only once fewer people are present to catch him out.

appraisal_events.evidence: Swann's specific questions about Vinteuil's life and what the little phrase might have meant to him go unanswered, since "ces gens... furent incapables d'y répondre."
appraisal_events.explanation: By contrast with the salon's empty posturing about the sonata, Swann's genuine, particular curiosity marks him locally as the only one with real discernment about the music.

status_effects.explanation: Her professed connoisseurship is exposed as stock phrase and evasion rather than genuine engagement.
His jargon-heavy praise is grouped with the salon's hollow, unanswerable admiration.
He is portrayed as a credulous disciple and a nervous novice reaching for borrowed sophistication.
His genuine, specific curiosity about the music contrasts favorably with the salon's inability to answer him.
